name: @macintacos/caret
description: A Claude Code plugin that replaces the terminal plan-approval prompt with a local web UI for inline review, annotation, and approval.

pinned.//: bun.lock is committed, so it is what pins every dependency exactly; a range above is the upgrade policy, not the resolved version. A bare version therefore means `bun update` must never move this one on its own, and these entries are the whole set. Everything else takes a range deliberately — zod and the TOML parser reading the config.toml trust boundary included: the lockfile already holds them, so a range costs no reproducibility and keeps them visible to an upgrade sweep. test/structure/exact-pin.test.ts fails on an exact pin with no reason, and on a reason that outlived its pin.
pinned.@pierre/diffs: Version-coupled to shiki through the resolve.alias block in ui/vite.config.ts, where an alias that stops matching grows the bundle by ~600 KB silently rather than failing anything. The pair moves as one reviewed bump, never on a sweep.
pinned.@pierre/trees: No stable release exists — the `latest` and `beta` dist-tags both point at the same prerelease. Exact rather than caret because a prerelease under a caret range is still a caret range: `^1.0.0-beta.6` expands to `>=1.0.0-beta.6 <2.0.0-0`, so a sweep would take a stable 1.0.0 the day it lands, and beta-to-stable is the jump that wants a human.

held.//: A dependency whose range deliberately stops below the current major, with the evidence for that and the condition that lifts it. Distinct from `pinned` above, which is about exact versions: an entry here names a range that is doing its job by excluding something. Unlike a pin, a held range is self-describing to `bun outdated` — it shows up as a major behind — so this block answers the question it raises rather than surfacing a decision nothing else would show.
held.typescript: Held at ^6 rather than 7.x (npm `latest` since 2026-07-08; the Go port). What breaks under 7.0.2 is two files: `tsc --noEmit` reports 50 errors and every one is inside test/structure/e2e-conventions.test.ts or test/structure/tokenize-conventions.test.ts — the only modules that import the compiler API — with src/, scripts/, opencode/ and the rest of test/ clean; those two then die at runtime on `ts.ScriptTarget` being undefined, because 7.x's package exports lib/version.cjs as `.` and moves the API behind ./unstable/* subpaths. Two of the four type-check consumers turn out not to consume it at all: `biome lint` passes because biome.jsonc enables no type-aware rules and biome carries its own parser, and bun strips types rather than checking them, so the rest of the unit suite never notices the move. What does block it is svelte-check, the only type-checker over the Svelte half. 4.7.5 hard-throws from bin/ts-version-check.js before checking anything once `typescript` is major >= 7, and 4.7.6, its current latest, declares the same `^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0` peer range. It does support 7.x behind `--tsgo`, but only with `typescript` kept at 6 and 7 aliased in as @typescript/native — a second install rather than a move, which leaves this range at ^6 either way. Re-run the trial when a svelte-check release type-checks Svelte against a plain `typescript@7`; test/structure/typescript-hold.test.ts reds when that peer range widens. Budget for re-shaping the two structure tests in the same pass — 7.x's unstable API exposes the guards and enums but no standalone parse, so they need more than a new import. Full evidence: EXC-1083.
